true_leverage.statement: Your true lever is the enjoyment-gated craft outlet — the single hidden Eating God in the year branch — because it is the only place in this chart where a very large internal supply of judgment turns into a finished thing an outsider can see.
true_leverage.why_not_others: Your other strengths are real but closed circuits. Companion and Direct Wealth sit jointly heaviest at the month pillar, where stem and branch both carry Companion force; that energy circulates among yourself and people like you — peers, equals, discussion partners — and returns as agreement, not as product. Your read on situations is sharp, but with Wealth tied up inside the peer circuit rather than flowing outward, a correct judgment left unshipped banks nothing. The Seven Killings pressure that would normally force structure from outside is thin here, so no external whip converts your conviction into deliverables. The Ren water day master is well supplied, so supply is never your constraint — routing is. That is why the lever is not 'be smarter' or 'network harder' but 'route through the one exit': the wood hidden in the year branch that quietly feeds the Eating God function. It opens only when the work pleases you, which makes it easy to miss and easy to starve — and exactly therefore it is the thing to protect.
true_leverage.evidence: Companion and Direct Wealth are jointly heaviest (nine each), stacked on the month pillar where stem and branch both carry Companion; the day master runs strong on abundant water; the Eating God exists only as hidden wood in the year branch; the luck sequence brings strong earth and fire only from the age-forty-nine and age-fifty-nine pillars onward, meaning external demand arrives late and must be met with a habit already built.

use_cases.scene: A peer discussion where you reach a strong read — say, a product decision, an investment thesis, or a technical judgment that everyone at the table ends up agreeing with.
use_cases.action: Before the discussion ends, attach one deliverable to your read: write the conclusion in one page — the decision, the reasoning, the next step — and send it to someone outside the peer circle within twenty-four hours. Your Companion-heavy structure means agreement inside the group feels like completion; it is not. The written page converts the peer circuit's output into the Eating God channel's input. If you leave the table with only the warm consensus, the water stays in the pond.
use_cases.behavior: You will notice the exact moment to act: when you hear yourself say the same judgment a second time with more confidence. That repetition is the signal that energy is circling; intercept it with a document, a prototype note, or a one-page memo addressed to a non-peer.

use_cases.scene: A stretch of assigned, dull work — tickets, reports, obligations someone else chose for you — filling your week.
use_cases.action: Batch the assigned work into fixed blocks and defend a daily ninety-minute block for self-chosen craft: the writing, building, or tuning you would do even unpaid. The output channel in this chart opens on enjoyment, so a week of pure assigned work produces zero shipped output no matter how many hours you log. Treat the self-chosen block as the day's real output and the assigned work as overhead to be cleared around it, not the other way round.
use_cases.behavior: The observable test: at the end of each day, ask what exists now that did not exist at breakfast — a draft, a working feature, a tuned piece. If the answer is 'I attended meetings and cleared queues', the gate stayed shut; if it is 'I moved the craft thing forward', the lever moved.

use_cases.scene: Choosing or negotiating a role, collaboration, or engagement — job offer, partnership, long-term client arrangement.
use_cases.action: Run the environment check before signing: does the arrangement require a finished deliverable from you on a fixed cycle, and is there a demand-carrier outside your friend group? Recruit at least one external demander — an editor, a paying client, a mentor with a stated deadline — who expects a finished thing from you on a date. This person manually supplies the Officer and Wealth functions your natal chart carries only thinly, and the late earth-and-fire luck pillars show your structure responds to exactly this shape of external pressure.
use_cases.behavior: In the negotiation itself, push for output-based terms — payment, credit, or evaluation attached to completed work rather than seniority or presence. When rewards attach to rank, you are paid for presence, which your structure supplies endlessly and worthlessly; when they attach to finished things, you are paid for what only the craft channel can produce.

next_90_days.one_thing: Ship one self-chosen craft project to an external audience. Pick a task you genuinely find interesting — not assigned, not negotiated — and carry it to a state where a stranger can see, hold, or buy it: a published piece, a live prototype, a signed deliverable. Pair it with the hard exit rule: every substantive peer conversation in these ninety days ends with one sentence written down — decision, owner, next step — before anyone leaves. These two moves route your existing effort through the only exit the chart has, instead of adding effort to a circuit that already returns agreement.
next_90_days.completion_signal: Verifiable by day ninety: one finished artifact exists under your name, accessible to people outside your peer circle at a link or in hand, plus a dated log showing at least twelve peer conversations closed with the written one-liner. If a stranger — not a friend — has received, reviewed, or paid for the artifact, the signal is fully met; if the artifact exists but only friends have seen it, the exit rule has been followed but the outlet has not, and the project does not count as shipped.
next_90_days.evidence: The chart's water supply is abundant and the day master runs strong, so more effort is not the bottleneck; the single Eating God exit in the year branch wood is. Ninety days of routing through that exit tests the mechanism directly, ahead of the earth-and-fire luck pillars that begin around age forty-nine and fifty-nine, when external demand finally runs strong and a shipping habit becomes the difference between arriving with something to hand over and arriving with conversation.

falsification_signals.signal: You complete the ninety-day protocol — the protected craft block, the written one-liners, the external audience — and observers outside your peer circle consistently rate the shipped work as unremarkable, or the work itself drains rather than feeds you.
falsification_signals.meaning: If finished output, repeatedly tested by non-peers, produces neither traction nor enjoyment, then the premise that the hidden Eating God is your viable exit does not hold in practice, and this manual's routing advice should be discarded in favor of structures that reward your peer-circuit strengths — judgment, coordination, consensus-building — directly.

falsification_signals.signal: Your environment changes shape: a role or partnership arrives that already contains a strong external demand-carrier with fixed deliverable cycles and output-attached rewards, and you find you perform well under it without any of the manual's scaffolding.
falsification_signals.meaning: If externally imposed structure alone unlocks consistent finishing — no protected blocks, no manual exit rules needed — then the constraint was always environmental, not chart-structural, and the leverage framing here was solving the wrong problem. Keep the environment; retire the manual. A chart reading describes tendencies under one environment; a different environment can make the entire mapping moot, and you should trust the observed run over the described one.
